jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellow in Economic Analysis of Nature Restoration Measures Across Different Farming Systems
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Fellow in Economic Analysis of Nature Restoration Measures Across Different Farming Systems

Are you interested in Economics of nature restoration in agriculture and can you contribute to the development of the Horizon Europe research project BALANCE? Then the Department of Environmental Science invites you to apply for a two-year Postdoc position. 

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two –year position from 1 May 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
• This section may include topics such as: 
• You will be contributing to/establishing/developing ... 
• You will be working primarily with ... 
• The position will focus on aspects of/elements of ... 
• You will be involved in ... 
• These activities will be in close collaboration with ...
The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to an interdisciplinary, EU-wide project investigating how nature restoration and nature-positive farming systems can contribute to biodiversity and farming. You will be working primarily with assessment of the short-, medium- and long-term costs and benefits of different nature restoration measures across different farming systems, with a focus on farm income, farm productivity and farm production. You will also develop methods for upscaling the findings on costs and benefits to the EU level. You will be involved in collaborations with researchers in agricultural and environmental economics as well as researchers in other disciplines and stakeholders collaborating in the same project.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in Environmental or Agricultural Economics or similar. Candidates should demonstrate strong skills in quantitative economics methods. Documented experience with farm economics and biodiversity is desirable.

We are looking for a candidate with:
• Strong analytical skills
• Experience in quantitative economic assessment related to agri-environmental challenges
• Experience in data collection from scientific articles and public and advisory reports 
• Demonstrated ability to publish scientific work in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English
• Ability to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:
• Experience in assessing environmental or agronomic topics across different spatial and time scales 
• Familiarity with policy-related research
• Experience in collaboration across disciplinary boundaries, particularly between natural and social sciences
We value motivated candidates with strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, who can engage constructively with researchers and stakeholders from different disciplinary and professional backgrounds. 

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technology at Aarhus University. The expertise ranges from economics, policy analysis, social science, and geography to physics, chemistry, microbiology and mathematical modelling. Both basic and applied research is conducted related to some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution, pollution control, land management, climate change, and energy systems, relevant to the quality of soil, water, air, biodiversity, and other ecosystem services. Advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders. Currently, about 170 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk/en/. The department is located at Risø Campus in Roskilde, 35 kilometers west of Copenhagen.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Environmental Social Science and Geography research unit. The unit employs approximately 25 staff, focusing on interdisciplinary analysis of the interlinkages between the environment and society from political science, economics and sociology perspectives. The strategic focus of the unit includes environmental policy development, regulation and instruments, understanding of actions and actors in policy formulation and implementation, spatially integrated modelling as well as policies and economics of ecosystem services and nature-based solutions. Research findings are used for dissemination to the research community, in advisory services to decision makers as well as for teaching.

Our ambition is to have an inclusive and open working environment. 

What we offer 
The department offers:

• an exciting interdisciplinary and international environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Katarina Elofsson, email katarina.elofsson@envs.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 10 January 2027 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.description:
Section of Epidemiology - Perinatal, Obstetric & Pediatric Epidemiology (POPE) group
Department of Public Health
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

Do you have a strong methodological foundation and an interest in designing, analysing and interpreting epidemiological observational studies? Do you enjoy working with large-scale datasets from national registries and cohort studies to address important public health questions? And would you like to contribute to research with high societal relevance, focusing on health and development from early childhood to adulthood?

If so, we invite you to apply for a full-time position (37 hours/week) as Staff Scientist in the Perinatal, Obstetric & Paediatric Epidemiology (POPE) Group at the Section of Epidemiology, University of Copenhagen, starting 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. In this role, you will execute analytical tasks within epidemiological research projects using national registry and cohort data, while developing and maintaining research data resources.

About Section of Epidemiology and the POPE group 

The Section of Epidemiology conducts research on determinants of health and disease across the life-course, with the aim of improving public health and advancing epidemiological theory.

You will join the POPE group, whose research focuses on maternal, child, and adolescent health from a life-course perspective. Our work examines how perinatal and early childhood exposures influence health outcomes throughout childhood and into young adulthood. Research topics include preterm birth, infections and vaccinations during pregnancy, mental health, and psychiatric treatment. The POPE group extensively uses Danish registry data and the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC), which provides rich self-reported and biological data. DNBC is a nationwide birth cohort including more than 96,000 individuals born in 1996-2003 whose mothers enrolled during pregnancy – more details here. The group is deeply involved in ongoing and future DNBC data collections, long-term follow-up, and international cohort collaborations. For more details read here: POPE

About the Department
The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

About the Position
The Staff Scientist will play a central role in advancing and executing epidemiological research within the POPE group. Working collaboratively with researchers, external collaborators, and colleagues across the Department of Public Health, with opportunities of conducting independent research, while the primary responsibility is to contribute and execute projects led by others based on large-scale Danish registry and cohort data. Responsibilities will include developing and maintaining research data resources, ensuring rigorous data quality, performing advanced analytical and statistical workflows, and contributing to the establishment/maintenance of data infrastructures that enable high-quality epidemiological research and peer-reviewed publications. The tasks include:

• 
Developing, maintaining, and quality assuring large-scale epidemiological data resources based on Danish national registries and cohort data including the DNBC.

• 
Contributing to the design, implementation, and conduct of epidemiological research projects by preparing analytical datasets, performing descriptive and statistical analyses, and supporting the interpretation and dissemination of findings.

• 
Coordinating key research activities related to the DNBC, including the ongoing 25-year follow-up and international federated analyses across cohorts.

• 
Establishing data set-ups where cohort data are embedded within register-based populations for resources beyond DNBC

• 
Providing methodological and analytical support to a broad range of epidemiological research projects within the group, contributing expertise in study implementation, data handling, troubleshooting and project development as needed.

• 
Taking responsibility for data security, exportation of analysis results, data governance and GDPR compliance within the POPE group

Profile and Qualifications

• 
Preferably a PhD in epidemiology and/or, public health or related fields.

• 
Advanced methodological and analytical skills, including demonstrated experience with data management, study design, statistical modelling, and interpretation of observational epidemiological data.

• 
A proven ability to envision, plan, and execute epidemiological research projects independently, while delivering work to agreed deadlines.

• 
Proven experience working with large and complex datasets from Danish national registries, large cohorts, or other longitudinal data sources using R, STATA and/or SAS.

• 
Strong scientific writing skills, with a track record of preparing and publishing peer-reviewed publications and project documentation.

• 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide expert methodological guidance and explain complex findings to researchers from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative fashion.

• 
Fluency in Danish (both written and spoken) is required, as the role involves working extensively with Danish national registry data and documentation.

• 
Experience in, or a strong interest in perinatal and life-course epidemiology, including research on child development, adolescent health, and/or mental health.

Place of employment
The place of employment is Section of Epidemiology, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen located near the city lakes in Central Copenhagen.

Terms of employment
The position is a full-time position (37 working hours weekly).
The starting date is 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on seniority with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experiences and qualifications.

Questions
For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor and Research group leader Katrine Strandberg-Larsen, email: ksla@sund.ku.dk. For questions regarding the recruitment procedure, please contact HR at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences: HR-IFSV@adm.ku.dk

Application
Your application must include the following:

• 
Cover letter, including motivations for applying for this position (max. 1 page).

• 
Curriculum Vitae, including education, work/research experience, language skills, and any other skills relevant to the position.

• 
A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education.

 Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply for position” below. Only online applications will be accepted.

Application deadline: 30 November 2026

We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Geotechnical Stability of Coastal Dikes - DTU Sustain
jobs.description:
Are you interested in starting your research career by contributing to the reduction of flooding risks associated with coastal dike instabilities?

Join DTU Sustain as a PhD candidate and perform pioneering research in slope stability, uncertainty characterisation and risk predictions.

As a PhD student, you will investigate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment of dikes, accounting for uncertainties in soil characterisation through modelling. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with slope stability analysis, statistical methods, physical modelling and risk assessment while addressing one of the pressing challenges of climate change in the built environment. 

You will become part of an ambitious and highly interdisciplinary research environment at DTU Sustain, collaborating closely with the Center for Coasts and Climate Adaptation, The Danish Environmental Protection Agency (formerly Danish Coastal Directorate) and Ghent University, while benefiting from access to state-of-the-art facilities in soil mechanics, geotechnical engineering and physical modelling. The position also includes international research stays with our collaborators, providing opportunities to develop a broad scientific network and gain hands-on experience with complementary expertise and facilities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate you will be responsible for developing, validating and implementing computational tools for the stability assessment in collaboration with team members, supervisors and international collaborators.

In detail your responsibilities will include:

• Implement and benchmark simplified limit equilibrium methods against advanced computational modelling for dike instabilities
• Assess the reliability of simplified and advanced slope stability methods
• Characterise and map the uncertainty of the soil conditions in coastal dikes
• Evaluate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment
• Publish high-quality research in leading international journals and present findings at international conferences.
• Contribute to courses and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment

The assessment of applications will be ongoing and will start before the application deadline.

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

jobs.occupation: Semiconductor process specialists - thin film deposition, plasma etching and characterisation - DTU Nanolab
jobs.description:
DTU Nanolab is looking for experienced engineers and physicists within thin film deposition, thin film plasma etching and thin film characterization in its ISO 4 & 5 cleanroom for micro- and nanofabrication.

We are seeking process specialists for the process specialist team. The team is responsible for thin-film deposition equipment (PVD, CVD, thermal processing), plasma etching systems, and a large suite of characterization tools (AFM, SEM, XRD, XPS, EDX, optical and stylus profilers, ellipsometers, reflectometers, PL mappers, and more). Responsibilities span the full equipment lifecycle, from procurement and implementation to documentation, maintenance, troubleshooting and the development of in-depth tool and process expertise needed to support users throughout a system's lifetime. 

The job
We are seeking people with experience and interest in plasma etching (ICP, IBE), plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD), AFM, sputter deposition, RTP annealing, PE-ALD, XRD and photo spectrometry. The job includes

• Process development of new processes and maintenance of current processes
• Documentation, including user manuals and process documentation
• In charge of QC and calibration procedures 
• Helping, training and education of users
• Assisting in fault finding in cooperation with technicians
• Assisting in procurement of new equipment: Specifications, demo runs and run-in
• Networking with other cleanroom labs in Europe
You will work closely with other process specialists and technicians in the Process Group, as well as with other DTU Nanolab groups, researchers, students and engineers from DTU and commercial companies. A large part of your working day will be spent in ISO 4 and 5 cleanrooms, where you will wear a full cleanroom suit.

Our expectations of you
You must have a M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree within either engineering or physics within a relevant field (micro/nanofabrication, experimental physics or similar) and have knowledge and experimental skills within the area of either plasma etching or thin film deposition and within different relevant characterization tools. 

Furthermore, we expect you to possess skills and qualifications in one or more of these areas:

• Plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD) and other CVD techniques (ALD and LPCVD)
• Plasma etching (ICP etching)
• PVD techniques (sputter deposition, e-beam evaporation and thermal evaporation)
• Thermal processing (oxidation, annealing and rapid thermal annealing)
• Thin film characterization techniques (AFM, XRD, photo spectrometry and other relevant)
• Hands-on experience working in a cleanroom environment
• Have a broad understanding of micro and nano processing
• Have an eye for detail and work meticulously
• Work well in teams with people from different backgrounds
• Service-minded
• Self-driven and able to plan your own working day
• Communicate well in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
At DTU Nanolab, safety is a top priority, and we are looking for candidates who can thrive in a highly safety-conscious environment and meet the following physical and mental requirements: Is able to work in an environment where it can be necessary to wear specialized safety and protective equipment. Is able to respond quickly and effectively in emergency situations, including evacuation in case of alarms. Is able to perform tasks that require work while standing up and mobility for longer periods.

What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international work environment. The work is highly hands-on and with a large degree of variation. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. Please note that this is not a research position, but a technical position, with a main focus to facilitate academic and industrial users within the field of thin film processing and characterization.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

Application and contact

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Operations, Leif Steen Johansen on +45 25 34 89 92 or lesjo@dtu.dk.

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Re-advertisement: Multi-physics modelling of wetting–drying induced ground movement, landslides and coastal erosion

Research area and project description
We are looking for a motivated and talented PhD candidate to join our multidisciplinary research team investigating climate-driven geohazards affecting infrastructure and the built environment. The successful candidate will become part of the long-term Villum Foundation research programme Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment (CEBE), bringing together researchers in geotechnical, structural, coastal and environmental engineering.

The PhD project focuses on developing a multi-physics platform to simulate the coupled hydromechanical behaviour of soil interacting with water in a geotechnical context. The overall objective is to establish a combination of numerical methods under the umbrella of multi-physics modelling to assess the stability of slopes and embankments subjected to wetting–drying cycles, changes in groundwater level and saturation, surface erosion from stormwater and debris, and toe erosion from waves in coastal environments.

The integrated modelling tool should describe the onset of slope instability, accounting for different hydroclimatic triggering factors (including variations induced by climate change scenarios), and the evolution of mass movement, considering large deformation. Therefore, different numerical methods may be combined, leveraging on the advantages of each approach for simulating a specific phase of the process. It is not the intent to develop new constitutive models for specific soil types, but it may be relevant to explore the use of meso-scale models for soils such as till and fissured clays, both native to Denmark. However, while the main application should be Danish soils, the numerical framework should be developed with versatility in mind to allow the assessment of climate-driven geohazards generally in urban and coastal regions.

Project description 
Applicants should submit a short research proposal (maximum 4 000 keystrokes) that demonstrates their understanding of the scientific challenge, identifies key knowledge gaps, formulates research objectives and hypotheses, outlines a possible methodological approach, and explains why their background makes them well-suited for the project. The proposal will be refined together with the supervisors during the PhD.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a BSc degree (180 ECTS) in civil engineering (or a closely related engineering discipline) and an MSc degree (minimum 90 ECTS) with a specialisation in geotechnical engineering, or computational engineering or coastal engineering, including advanced coursework in numerical methods, finite element analysis, and geotechnical engineering.

Further requirements:
• Excellent communication skills in spoken and written English are required.
• Applicants are expected to have experience in numerical modelling.
• Demonstrated programming skills (e.g. Python, MATLAB, Fortran, C++, or a similar scientific programming language) are required.
Place of employment and place of work

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Methods for design of biobased building enclosure systems with a regenerative environmental impact

Research area and project description
The objective of this Ph.D. project is to define methods for design of building enclosure systems following a paradigm for obtaining a regenerative environmental impact. The project aims to define a gated process for design of such systems and demonstrate its operationalisation in the actual development of building systems in collaboration with producers and companies in the building industry.

The methodological approach will be a combination of co-creation techniques where the Ph.D. student actively engages with the building industry to develop practical and useful design methods and workflows that leads to a regenerative environmental performance of building systems. The work is centered around the use of biobased materials in systems with longevity in terms of building physics. Concepts of circularity is expected to be a lever for this.

The background for the project is that the planetary boundaries are overstepped due to excessive environmental load from human activities which means that humanity has entered a zone of risk of deleterious or even catastrophic environmental change at continental to global scales. The main driver for this is the built environment that e.g. accounts for approx. 43% of all energy-related CO2-emissions. There is therefore an acute need to reduce the environmental load from the built environment to a level that enables the regenerative properties of the planetary ecosystems to reestablish the safe operating space below the planetary boundaries.

Qualifications and specific competences
The candidate must have a technical background in building science such as B.Sc. or B.Eng. or similar. Applicants must furthermore have a technical master’s degree or at least one year of master’s degree in building science, environmental performance of buildings or similar topics. Documented skills in application of life-cycle assessments for buildings, hygrothermal performance simulations, and computer programming is mandatory. Experience in heat and moisture measurements in relation to buildings is preferred but not required.

jobs.description:
SDU Mechanical Engineering (SDU ME), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for an 18-month postdoctoral position in thermodynamics-based whole-ship energy modelling. The position is expected to start in March 2027, with the specific start date to be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

 

What we offer

You will join a research project titled Thermodynamics-Based Whole-Ship Energy Mapping for Retrofit-Oriented Maritime Decarbonization (STERN) funded by Den Danske Maritime Fond. STERN addresses a practical maritime engineering challenge: improvements to individual components do not necessarily result in optimal energy performance for the vessel as a whole. The project will develop physically consistent steady-state and dynamic energy models to quantify interactions among propulsion, auxiliary equipment, cooling and heating systems, waste heat and energy storage under representative operating conditions.

The postdoc will work within an interdisciplinary SDU team led by Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur, together with Professor Marie Lützen and Associate Professor Paride Gullo, and collaborate with maritime partners including the shipping company Hafnia, DESMI and Fredericia Maskinmesterskole (FMS). ShippingLab will support maritime knowledge exchange and outreach. The position offers opportunities for independent scientific development, high-quality publications and close interaction with industry.

 

Main research activities

• 
Develop modular steady-state thermodynamic and energy-balance models for whole-ship energy mapping, covering fuel input, propulsion, auxiliary power, thermal loads, heat rejection and recoverable energy streams.

• 
Extend these models to dynamic energy simulations representing time-varying engine loads, operational profiles, mode transitions and relevant subsystem interactions.

• 
Model and analyze selected marine subsystems and energy-integration pathways, including propulsion-related energy demand, waste heat recovery, HVAC, cooling/heating optimization, thermal storage and battery storage.

• 
Use representative vessel and component data, engineering correlations and partner feedback to check model assumptions, quantify uncertainty and compare baseline and retrofit-oriented scenarios in terms of energy use and emissions.

• 
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, project meetings, reporting and dissemination of non-confidential results.

 

Required qualifications

• 
A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Thermal Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline (completed by the date of employment).

• 
A strong foundation in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics (thermo-fluids) and energy-system analysis.

• 
Demonstrated experience in numerical thermodynamic or energy-system modelling, including steady-state analysis and time-dependent/dynamic simulation.

• 
Programming or modelling skills in MATLAB, Python or comparable scientific computing environments, with the ability to develop and document reproducible models.

• 
Knowledge of waste heat recovery, refrigeration/HVAC, cooling and heating networks, energy storage or component performance maps.

• 
Ability to conduct independent research, work with an interdisciplinary team and communicate research results effectively in English.

 

Qualifications considered an advantage

• 
Experience with marine engines, propulsion systems, ship energy systems or vessel operating profiles.

• 
Experience with dynamic simulation and control environment like MATLAB Simulink, Modelica/Dymola or equivalent modelling frameworks can also be considered.

• 
Knowledge of advanced control engineering, optimization or model-based control approaches, and experience collaborating with industrial partners.

 

Workplace description 

The position is full-time at SDU ME and located at the SDU main campus in Odense. SDU Odense is the university’s largest campus and provides a strong framework for interdisciplinary research, teaching, and innovation. You will be part of a modern workplace with high professionalism, strong academic communities, and a commitment to diversity and equal opportunities. SDU also offers dedicated support for International Staff. Learn more about careers and work life at SDU here: Careers at SDU.

SDU ME is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME) at the Faculty of Engineering. The research activities at SDU ME span widely from fluid mechanics, multi-physics simulation and optimization to condition monitoring and structural dynamics, composite materials, mechanical design, and naval architecture and marine engineering. 

The research environment combines thermo-fluid science, energy engineering and computational modelling, with collaboration across SDU and external maritime partners. The successful candidate will contribute to an industry-informed research project while working closely with academic colleagues and maritime experts. The research group is also part of the broader maritime research community at SDU, providing opportunities for transdisciplinary collaboration across faculties through the SDU Maritime Centre.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Odense. 

 

Further information

Application

Assessment and selection process

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

SDU Centre for Software Technology in Vejle, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within interaction technology and AI engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates.

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

• 
be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

• 
join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

• 
have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Software Technology is research and education in software engineering, interactive technology and artificial intelligence. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and interactive software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how AI technologies and data-informed software development with a human-centred perspective can change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

Interactive Systems Engineering

• 
AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field, such as CHI (Human Factors in Computing Systems), DIS (Designing Interactive Systems), CSCW (Computer-Supported Cooperative Work), NordiCHI, UIST (User Interface Software & Technology), IUI, HRI (Human-Robot Interaction), TEI (Tangible Embedded Embodied Interaction), IDC (Interaction Design & Children), UbiComp (Ubiquitous Computing), PerCom, EICS, AAAI, WWW, ACM CIKM; and in journals such as IMWUT and IEEE TASE. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline, completed before the application deadline. 

For the tenure-track assistant professor positions we expect at least one year of research experience beyond the PhD, gained in academia, at a research institute or in industry. Applicants must demonstrate a higher level of achievement in research and related professional activities than generally expected of assistant professor applicants, as well as the potential to attain international research excellence within their field and meet the criteria for employment as an associate professor during the tenure track assistant professorship.

For the associate professor positions we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense and Sønderborg and with the new centre also in Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

Hear about the vision behind SDU Vejle - and why you as a researcher should consider joining the journey.

Curious?

If you are interested in learning more about the position, please contact:

Tenure Track at the Faculty of Engineering, SDU
The Faculty of Engineering at SDU offers an attractive tenure track programme aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.
